summary.text: Davina Duerr is a Democratic member of the Washington House of Representatives for District 1-Position 1, where she has served since 2019, and she is running for re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election against Maggie Wang.
An architect, she previously served on the Bothell City Council.

paragraphs.text: Duerr was born in 1971, the daughter of a Taiwanese immigrant, grew up in Upstate New York and graduated from Syracuse University with a bachelor's degree in architecture and a minor in environmental geography, according to Wikipedia.
She works as a senior interior architect at an architecture firm in Bellevue, Washington, according to the same article.

Before entering the Legislature, Duerr served on the Bothell Landmarks Preservation Board for ten years and co-founded the M.I.L.K. Money Project, which provides academic and financial services to underprivileged students.
She served on the Bothell City Council from 2016 to 2019, including as deputy mayor.
Duerr was appointed to the House in July 2019 to fill the seat vacated by Derek Stanford, who had been appointed to the state Senate, and was elected to a full term in November 2020.
Ballotpedia lists her as winning the general elections of 2020, 2022 and 2024, and as advancing from the August 4, 2026 primary with 74.2 percent of the vote.
Ballotpedia lists her 2023-2024 committee assignments as Environment & Energy, Local Government (as chair) and Transportation.
